verdict_reason: The real-mode check fails open on a reply without a missing list, and the stub check sits outside the stub module.

todos.issue: realCall returns (await checkSpecies(lines)).missing ?? [], so a reference-data reply without a missing array (a contract drift, a proxy or gateway answering 200 with another body) reads as 'every species listed' and the submission check passes without having checked anything, silently. reference-data's SpeciesCheckResponse always sets missing (List.copyOf), so the fallback never helps a valid reply; it only fails open on an invalid one.
todos.fix: Must: a species-check reply without a missing array is treated as reference data failing (503 via callReferenceData), never as all species listed. One way: return checkSpecies(lines).then(({ missing }) => { if (!Array.isArray(missing)) throw new Error('Species check reply has no missing list'); return missing }) and add a real-mode test for a reply of {}.

todos.issue: The stub's species check (listedInStub, reading COMMODITY_GROUPS) lives in species-check.js, while the stub's search (searchCommodities) lives in stub.js, the module that owns the stub catalogue. Stub behaviour now has two homes, and species-check.js reaches into the stub's data rather than calling a stub function as search.js does.
todos.fix: Must: stub.js owns every stub answer over COMMODITY_GROUPS, and species-check.js calls it the same way search.js calls searchCommodities. One way: move listedInStub into stub.js as an exported unlistedLinesInStub(lines) and use stubCall: () => unlistedLinesInStub(lines).
